structure: A single short Markdown ruling file, 71 lines (workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-ian-2026-11-16.md), from Ian, dated 16 November 2026, on whether the consignor party picker must also list addresses saved for an exporter role. It has four sections: a title paragraph that names the question and quotes the judge's challenge raised while reviewing inc-087 in the consignment-parties theme; "What was asked", which quotes inc-087's acceptance criterion 2 verbatim with its three citations and then sets out the code evidence that no exporter role exists (the address book's six-role vocabulary, an empty grep for EXPORTER, holdsRole taking a single role, each party binding exactly one addressBookRole); "Decided", five numbered points; and "What this changes in the backlog", four bullets. Scope is the whole file and nothing is left out. At 71 lines with every word load-bearing it is well inside one agent's reading, so it is one part.

parts.title: Whole ruling
parts.scope: The whole file: the opening question with the judge's quoted challenge, the criterion and code evidence under "What was asked", the five numbered points under "Decided", and the four bullets under "What this changes in the backlog". There is no other part.
covers: The opening: the question put, whether the consignor party picker must also list addresses saved for an exporter role, raised by the judge reviewing inc-087 in the consignment-parties theme, and the challenge quoted ("Where did that acceptance criteria come from? The v4 or the prototype? If the role doesn't exist...")

What was asked: inc-087 acceptance criterion 2 as quoted, both halves — the consignor picker listing consignor-role addresses together with exporter-role ones, and the five party sections Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination — with its three citations (prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-064, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-137, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116)

What was asked: the code evidence that no exporter role exists — the address book's whole role vocabulary PLACE_OF_ORIGIN, CONSIGNOR, PLACE_OF_DESTINATION, CONSIGNEE, IMPORTER, BRANCH_ADDRESS at tests:domain/shared/constants/address-types.ts:20-27; grep -rn "EXPORTER" over repos/trade-imports-address-book/src/main/java/ returning nothing; holdsRole taking a single role at frontend:src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:22-23; each party binding exactly one addressBookRole at frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/parties.js:13-50

Decided point 1: the exporter clause of inc-087's criterion 2 is dropped — not deferred, not handed to another theme, not a reason to add a role; there is no exporter role, there never was one, and none is to be created for this

Decided point 2: it was an identifiable distillation error, both prototype claims behind the clause being the prototype's own internal type vocabulary rather than a domain role — prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-064 (verbatim, app/routes.js:3851-3876) quoting 'consignor-or-exporter': ['consignor-or-exporter', 'consignor', 'exporter'], and prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-137 (inferred, app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:15-28) quoting id: 'consignor-or-exporter', heading: 'Consignor'; the second being barred by ruling:ian-2026-11-11 point 2 as a demo fixture that is "evidence of nothing except what the prototype happened to hard-code", and the first being app/routes.js, the prototype's routing glue, the same thing one level further in

Decided point 3: the third citation on the same line is the one that refuses the clause — ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116 quoting Sam that "Prototype is the authority for how things look and feel not how they are architected", with its statement that the address record's field shape for address uses and roles is the address book service's design; a role vocabulary is architecture, so the criterion cited the rule that forbids it beside the claims that broke it

Decided point 4: what the prototype actually says is already built — consignor-or-exporter expresses that one section covers both parties, with no separate exporter section and the heading reading "Consignor"; that is look and feel, within the prototype's authority, and the real service already models it as the single CONSIGNOR role; the criterion's second half (five party sections, no exporter among them) is satisfied by inc-087, so the row is correct as built and needs no further work

Decided point 5: adding an EXPORTER role would be the wrong fix — it would split a party the design deliberately merged and put work on the address-book theme that no requirement asks for; no row in any theme is to add one

What this changes in the backlog: inc-087's open question is answered and cleared and the row stays done with nothing rebuilt; no requirement changes state and the ruling adopts nothing new, removing a clause no source supported; the address-book theme is handed nothing, and a future re-distil re-drafting the exporter clause from the same two prototype claims is refused by this ruling

What this changes in the backlog, the general point: ruling:ian-2026-11-11 point 2 bars app/data/*.js as a source of data, this case shows the same files read for a rule (kind: rule, not kind: data) and reaching a criterion anyway, and the bar is on what the file is, not on how the claim is labelled
Any question the file only floats rather than decides, and anything it clearly leaves open on what it touches, recorded as a gap claim rather than a decision
